newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Ex-Zaire says Barrick gold area under review.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Zaire says Barrick gold area under review.

text.p: The mining minister in Laurent Kabila's Democratic Republic of Congo on Tuesday said a huge concession leased by Barrick Gold Corporation was one of several old contracts under review.
"The problem with Barrick is that we still have to sort out the lease, we are still making proposals and waiting for a response," Minister of Mines Matukulo Kambale told Reuters in an interview.
"If the agreement is good we change nothing...if we see something wrong like with these people, we suggest that some changes be made. If they accept OK, we ratify that, if they don't, OK."
He would not say what changes to the lease the government, which has been in power for two weeks, was asking for.
The Barrick mining concession, which was negotiated under ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko, covers an area of over 80,000 sq km near Bunia in the northeastern corner of the former Zaire.

Kambale said a preliminary deal for gold exploration had been signed on Tuesday with Russell Resources Group over a large area near Bunia. He did not make clear whether there was any overlap with the Barrick concession.
"It is not good to have very huge concessions in the hands of one company, it is better for more companies to have a chance," said Kambale.
